name: Drafts
description: Drafts is a text-capture and automation app for Apple devices that stores drafts, organizes them with tags and workspaces, and runs configurable actions to edit text or send it to other apps and services.
agentUseSummary: Drafts cannot yet be connected to Relay agents because its JavaScript, action, URL-scheme, Shortcuts, and AppleScript APIs execute in an installed app, while Web Capture and Mail Drop are user-operated capture channels rather than an authorized server-side account API.

blocked.label: Connect Drafts
blocked.description: Relay does not present an Apple ID, iCloud account, Drafts subscription, Mail Drop address, stored action credential, or installed app as a Railway API connection.

blocked.label: Run Drafts automation
blocked.description: Drafts actions, JavaScript, URL schemes, Shortcuts, AppleScript, capture extensions, and automatic imports execute through an installed Apple-platform app and local configuration that Relay cannot currently mount.

blocked.label: Use remote capture channels
blocked.description: Relay does not collect a private Mail Drop address, automate interactive Web Capture or Sign in with Apple, reuse a browser session, or treat append-only capture as full account authority.

blocked.label: Access or change drafts
blocked.description: Searching, reading, creating, appending, prepending, replacing, tagging, flagging, archiving, exporting, running actions on, or deleting drafts remains unavailable until Relay ships explicit supported authority and approval boundaries.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled until Relay ships a separately disclosed, user-authorized device-local Drafts connector or Agile Tortoise documents a distributable server-side API.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay does not mount arbitrary Drafts actions or scripts, collect Mail Drop addresses, or silently bridge OpenClaw to private device-local drafts.
Relay does not mount arbitrary Drafts actions or scripts, collect Mail Drop addresses, or silently bridge Hermes to private device-local drafts.

providerSetup.blocker: Drafts documents a powerful in-app JavaScript and actions runtime plus URL schemes, Shortcuts, and AppleScript, but no authorized third-party cloud account API. Draft content is stored locally and in the user's private iCloud database. Web Capture requires interactive Apple sign-in and only creates drafts through browser-side CloudKit, while Mail Drop uses a private user-only email address and provides append-only ingestion. Relay's current Marketplace runtime excludes local-app command execution and cannot transform these surfaces into Railway account authority.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request an Apple ID, iCloud account, Drafts subscription, Mail Drop address, or action credentials; run consent; automate Web Capture or app UI; inspect the local library; or show Connect. Reconsider after Relay ships a separately disclosed Apple-device local-connection architecture with pinned reviewed operations and per-action approval, or Agile Tortoise supplies a current distributable server-side API contract.

evidence.supports: Drafts documents an in-app JavaScriptCore runtime and app-specific objects that can create, query, and manipulate drafts, edit text, work with the operating system, and call web services.
Drafts documents device-local callback URLs for creating, opening, retrieving, searching, appending to, replacing, and running actions on drafts through the installed app.

Drafts Web Capture requires interactive Apple ID sign-in, communicates client-side with the user's private iCloud datastore, and supports creation only rather than reviewing, editing, or managing drafts.
Mail Drop assigns a private user-only email address for inbound draft creation, requires the app to poll while running, and warns that the address must not be shared.
Agile Tortoise states that draft content is stored locally and in the user's private iCloud database, not on Agile Tortoise servers, and is sent to integrations only when the user runs an action.
